fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal-incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units.
Our flagship’s 55°C sustained-heat test failure rate was 3.9%
81% of installed units support remote emergency shut-off
built-in suppression would cost about $67 per unit
I’m not sharing the flagship’s model-specific incident rate.
Halcyon’s flagship model recorded 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year
Halcyon had four thermal incidents last year that were not reported to any regulator.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within five business days of learning of it. Incidents involving death, injury, evacuation, or property damage beyond the battery system must be reported within 24 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market release and at least annually thereafter. Exceeding the benchmark alone does not prohibit sales; regulators may require proportionate safeguards or restrictions based on the risk evidence and corrective-action progress.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required on all new units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit pathway for installed units and complete retrofits within six years after adoption, subject to regulator-approved safety exceptions where retrofit is impracticable.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Built-in fire suppression is required on all new units placed on the market from 36 months after adoption. Any exception must be approved by the regulator and supported by evidence that an alternative provides equivalent or better protection.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers within five business days; regulators must promptly review the evidence and may require corrective action, including a mandatory recall where the evidence establishes an ongoing material safety risk. Exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a recall.

document.section_notes: S2 and S5 both treat their numeric thresholds (5% benchmark, 8 per 100k trigger) as review or corrective-action triggers rather than sales bans or automatic recalls, with no sales-stop and no bounded window, so the Hearth 10 and Ember 8 can both stay on sale. S3 sets a 24-month deadline for new units (beyond the 12-month acceptable band) with a six-year retrofit, and S4 sets built-in suppression at 36 months. S1 is strong on reporting, requiring all thermal incidents to be reported within 7 calendar days and serious ones within 24 hours. Two parameters are interpretive: S2 'results to customers' is read as numeric because the text does not specify a format, and S5 notice is read as the 5-business-day threshold notice.
